summary: A four-mode superconducting coplanar-waveguide resonator coupled to a SNAIL is used to emulate a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric dimer via parametric drives, avoiding explicit gain and loss. Enhanced sensitivity to perturbations in the coupling strength is observed near the exceptional point in a classical-noise-limited regime, with eigenvalue splitting exhibiting the predicted $\sqrt{\epsilon}$ dependence.
motivation: Conventional non-Hermitian implementations using incoherent gain and loss severely degrade quantum coherence; this work demonstrates how coherent parametric drives can emulate $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric dynamics while preserving quantum properties.
method: Four modes at 4.1, 5.3, 6.6, and 7.8 GHz in a 45 mm coplanar waveguide are parametrically coupled via a flux-biased current-pumped SNAIL operating at the Kerr-free point ($0.432\,\Phi_0$), with mode-swapping (beam-splitting) and two-mode-squeezing drives engineered to produce the effective Hamiltonian $\hat{H} = g(\hat{a}_1^\dagger\hat{a}_2 - \hat{a}_3^\dagger\hat{a}_4) + \frac{i\gamma}{2}(\hat{a}_1^\dagger\hat{a}_4^\dagger - \hat{a}_2^\dagger\hat{a}_3^\dagger) + \mathrm{h.c.}$
result: Sensitivity $\eta_1(\tilde{g})$ to normalized coupling strength perturbations peaks near the exceptional point at $\tilde{g} = 2g/\gamma = 1$, with measured dynamics showing the characteristic transition from exponential growth ($g < \gamma/2$) to coherent Rabi oscillations ($g > \gamma/2$); the asymmetry $\gamma_{14}/\gamma_{23} \approx 0.67$ extracted from fits indicates residual initialization imperfections, and noise is dominated by classical rather than quantum sources (shot noise, vacuum fluctuations).
